## Useful quadrilateral properties {#fv2-quadrilaterals .fv-lesson .proof-lesson }

```{=html}
<div class="proof-properties"><div><h3>Trapezium</h3><p>One pair of opposite sides parallel.</p></div><div><h3>Kite</h3><p>Two pairs of adjacent sides equal; diagonals perpendicular.</p></div><div><h3>Parallelogram</h3><p>Opposite sides equal and parallel; diagonals bisect each other.</p></div><div><h3>Rhombus</h3><p>All sides equal; a parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals.</p></div><div><h3>Rectangle</h3><p>A parallelogram with right angles and equal diagonals.</p></div><div><h3>Square</h3><p>A rectangle with all sides equal.</p></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §2.2.2 · pp. 18–19</div>

::: {.notes}
A concise reference to properties used in proofs. The booklet contains additional angle and area properties. Know what is given and what must be established: do not quote the perpendicular diagonals of a rhombus when that is exactly what Example 2.5 asks you to prove. The trapezium convention follows the supplied booklet.
:::
